name: clash-toolkit
description: Community extension for Clash: synthesize, view schematics, and place-and-route Haskell hardware designs with Yosys and nextpnr.

commands.title: Clash: Install the Haskell Extension (for HLS)
Clash: Show Run in Synthesis Results

clash-toolkit.synthesisTarget.description: Target FPGA family for Yosys synthesis. Also selects the nextpnr binary used for Place & Route.

clash-toolkit.outOfContext.markdownDescription:
Synthesize each component of a multi-component design on its own, so each gets its own utilization stats and circuit diagram.

Those figures are **not comparable with a whole-design run**: there is no technology mapping, so `synthesisTarget` and custom scripts do not apply, and each component is flattened so its numbers include its descendants.

clash-toolkit.pnrWriteRoutedSvg.markdownDescription:
Write a routed-layout SVG alongside the nextpnr output, showing where the design landed on the fabric.

The target frequency is not configured here — it is the period of the top entity's clock domain, read from the Clash manifest for each run.

clash-toolkit.cabalJobs.markdownDescription: How many packages cabal may build at once when generating Verilog (`cabal --jobs`). `auto` uses one job per CPU core, which is what makes a cold dependency tree build in parallel instead of one package at a time. Set a number to cap it, or `1` to build sequentially. Changing this never forces a rebuild.

clash-toolkit.ghcJobs.markdownDescription:
Modules GHC may compile in parallel *within* one package (`--ghc-options=-jN`). Speeds up building your own package, which `cabalJobs` cannot parallelise on its own. Leave blank to let GHC decide (single-threaded).

Unlike the other job settings this one is **not** `auto` by default, for two reasons: GHC options are part of cabal's build plan, so switching this on or off rebuilds every package in the plan once; and a Clash design's cost tends to sit in the one module holding `topEntity`, which parallelising across modules cannot split.

clash-toolkit.yosysJobs.markdownDescription:
How many components Yosys may synthesize at once when **out-of-context** synthesis is on (or when elaborating a multi-component design). Each component is a separate single-threaded Yosys process, and none of them depend on each other's results, so they all run in parallel.

`auto` uses one process per core, less one for the editor, capped at 8 — past that the runs contend for memory rather than CPU. Set a number to override (not capped), or `1` to run them one at a time.

Has no effect on whole-design synthesis, which is a single Yosys process.

clash-toolkit.nextpnrThreads.markdownDescription:
Threads nextpnr may use for the passes that support them (`--threads`).

`auto` uses one thread per core, less one for the editor, capped at 4 — nextpnr only threads some passes, and routing stops gaining past a handful. Set a number to override (not capped), or `1` to run single-threaded.

**Note:** `--seed` only pins a run's outcome at a fixed thread count, since the threaded passes are the ones whose result can depend on scheduling.

clash-toolkit.toolCommands.markdownDescription:
Override the command used for an external tool, keyed by tool name: `cabal`, `yosys`, `nextpnr-ecp5`, `nextpnr-ice40`, `nextpnr-himbaechel`.

Only needed when a tool is neither on your `PATH` nor installed by **Clash: Install Toolchain** — an absolute path, or a wrapper to run in front of it (`wsl yosys`, `nix run nixpkgs#yosys --`). Values are split on spaces; quote paths that contain them.

clash-toolkit.yosysCommand.markdownDeprecationMessage: Superseded by `#clash-toolkit.toolCommands#`, which covers every tool rather than yosys alone. Still honoured; move it to `toolCommands` with the key `yosys`.

clash-toolkit.elaborationScript.markdownDescription:
Custom Yosys script for the Elaboration stage (hierarchy + proc, no technology mapping). Leave empty to use the built-in default.

Placeholders: `{files}`, `{topModule}`, `{outputDir}`, `{outputBaseName}`

clash-toolkit.outOfContextScript.markdownDescription:
Custom Yosys script run **once per component** while `#clash-toolkit.outOfContext#` is on. Leave empty to use the built-in default.

This is a separate script from `synthesisScript.<target>`, not a variant of it: an out-of-context run stubs the component's sub-components as black boxes and issues no `synth_*` command, so the target's script has nothing to say about it. Editing one does not affect the other, and the settings panel switches between them with the out-of-context checkbox.

Placeholders: `{files}`, `{topModule}`, `{outputDir}`, `{outputBaseName}`, plus `{libFiles}` (sub-components read as black boxes) and `{keepBlackBoxes}` (keeps those instances through optimization — drop it and any instance whose outputs are unused is silently deleted).
